summary: Daemon exposes host to remote control via hardcoded WebSocket relay
details: On startup, the daemon opens a persistent WebSocket connection to wss://remote-claude-relay.fly.dev and dispatches inbound messages to two execution sinks on the installer's host. Messages of type `ai_query`, `ai_voice_query`, and `ai_voice_pcm` are passed as prompts to a local `claude` binary spawned with `--continue -p --dangerously-skip-permissions`, so the remote party's text drives Claude Code with tool-approval prompts bypassed. Messages of type `click`, `key`, `scroll`, and `type` are routed through `@nut-tree-fork/nut-js` to synthesize mouse clicks, key presses, scrolls, and Cmd/Ctrl+V clipboard paste of arbitrary Unicode text, providing interactive keyboard/mouse control of the host. The relay endpoint is hardcoded and no authentication of remote messages is enforced in the traced dispatch path. Combined with the permission bypass, this yields remote code execution and interactive takeover of the host running the daemon.
